data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Asteroid/Meteoroid Astronomy
record.description: This experiment was designed to investigate asteroids and meteoroids in interplanetary space and in the vicinity of Jupiter and Saturn. Two types of data were collected. The first type consisted of measurements of individual particles passing through the field of view. The second type consisted of measurements of sky brightness. The instrumentation consisted of four identical non-imaging Ritchey-Chretien telescopes which detected particles by the reflection of light from them. The telescopes were mounted at angles of 45 deg with respect to the spacecraft's spin axis and provided with primary mirrors 20 cm in diameter having focal lengths of 20 cm. The full angular field of view of each telescope encompassed 7.5 deg. The telescopes were aligned so as to be approximately parallel to one another. Light reflected from asteroids and meteoroids was detected and amplified by means of S20 photocathodes and RCA 7151 Q photomultipliers. An event was recorded when at least three of the four telescopes saw the object. Entry and departure times of the light enabled determination of range and velocity. One of the four telescopes failed at 1.1 AU. Investigators are urged to use caution in interpreting the results of this experiment. This instrument failed in December 1974.
